newsitem.title: CHINA: China's CITIC says 1996 profits at 2.47 bln yuan.
newsitem.headline: China's CITIC says 1996 profits at 2.47 bln yuan.

text.p: China International Trust and Investment Corp (CITIC) said on Monday it posted 2.474 billion yuan ($298 million) in profits last year, up 21 percent from 1995.

The Beijing-based company, which is supervised by China's State Council or cabinet, also said that Zhang Xiao, former president of China's state-run Industrial and Commercial Bank, had been named vice chairman.
CITIC said in a statement that its total assets reached 191.5 billion yuan at the end of 1996, an increase of 14.9 percent over the previous year.
The conglomerate has interests ranging from banking and securities to real estate, telecommunications and manufacturing and controls the Hong Kong-listed Citic Pacific.
CITIC, which has said it wants to become more of a financial service company, said its financial operations recorded stable growth last year.
It said its CITIC Industrial Bank unit made good profits while it expanded operations.
Its CITIC Securities Co operations evaded risk problems after a reorganisation and the firm was active in the areas of share issuance, fund management and financial advisory services, it said.
CITIC's profits in the industrial sector had gone up after it readjusted existing assets and increased investment in the power, telecommunications and automotive sectors, it said.
Progress was made in CITIC's overseas operations, with purchases of New Zealand timberland expected to become one of its largest overseas natural resources investment projects, it said.
The group would work to earn a name as one of the world's most influential financial and industrial corporations by the year 2000, it said but gave no further details.
The 1996 results were announced by CITIC chairman Wang Jun at a meeting of the board of directors on March 9, it said.
Zhang's appointment, decided in early February by the State Council, was also announced by Wang at the meeting, it said.
